newsitem.title: USA: Bio-Vascular to spin off Vital Images.
newsitem.headline: Bio-Vascular to spin off Vital Images.

text.p: Bio-Vascular Inc said Tuesday its board had approved the spin-off to shareholders of its Vital Images subsidiary.
The spin-off, pending review of appropriate filings by the Securities and Exchange Commission, is expected to be completed by the end of next March.
At that time, Vital Images will trade as an independent public company.
Bio-Vascular said it attempted to structure the deal as a tax-free transaction. But no assurance can be given about the final tax treatment, it added.
In the spin-off, it expects one share of Vital Images to be distributed for every two Bio-Vascular shares held.
Prior to the spin-off, Bio-Vascular will make a contribution to Vital Images, which is currently estimated at $3.3 million in intercompany debt and $10 million in cash for working capital.
Cash and equivalents retained by Bio-Vascular are estimated at $19 million.
The company also said Vincent Argiro, chief technology officer of Vital Images and founder of the unit, will divest shares of Bio-Vascular to bring his ownership in the company to under five percent.
Argiro, a vice president of Bio-Vascular, currently owns about 5.6 percent of the company.
The reduction in Argiro's holdings increases the likelihood that the spin-off will be deemed a tax-free transaction.

Bio-Vasculuclar develops, makes and markets proprietary specialty medical products for use in thoracic, cardiac, neuro and vascular surgery. Vital Images develops software for medical research, clinical diagnosis and surgical planning.

"We also expect that both companies would benefit from the stock market's preference for 'pure play' and highly focused companies, one in medical software and services, the other in medical devices, leading over time to a fuller valuation of each," John Karcanes, president and chief executive officer of Bio-Vascular, said in a statement.
He said Vital Images has developed a new clinical diagonstic product that is more powerful, has increased flexibility and is easier to use. The product will be ready to ship early in 1997.
